newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to award 4th mobile licence on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Germany to award 4th mobile licence on Tuesday.

text.p: The German government confirmed on Monday that it would award the fourth mobile phone licence on Tuesday at a news conference with Post and Telecommunications Minister Wolfgang Boetsch.

Although the government has given no information about candidates for the licence, it has been widely believed in the industry that diversified utility Viag AG was the only company to have applied for the concession.
The government will hold a news conference to announce the winner of the licence and the details of its terms at 1100 GMT.
The licence regulates operation of a digital cellular mobile phone network based on the DCS 1800 personal communications network standard.

The so-called E2 licence would be the second mobile phone network built based on this standard. The first is operated by the E-Plus consortium which is owned by Veba AG, Thyssen AG BellSouth and Vodafone.

There are two other digital cellular operators -- Mannesmann Mobilfunk GmbH's D2 network and the D1 network of Deutsche Telekom AG. These networks are based on the Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) standard.
